title: Aleph Readiness Report (warm phase: readiness)
description: The gate between collecting context and publishing conclusions, produced by warm phase 7. Readiness answers one question: has Aleph gathered enough of the right kinds of material to say anything at all about this document yet? The whole file exists to make a refusal possible and legible. A system that always produces an answer will, whenever the evidence is thin, produce a confident-sounding one - and the confidence will be the model's, not the evidence's. Aleph forbids that substitution structurally: MODEL CONFIDENCE MUST NEVER STAND IN FOR MISSING EVIDENCE. A high model_confidence over an insufficient evidence base does not raise readiness, does not unlock publication, and must never be displayed as reassurance; the only cure for a gap is retrieval. Every dimension therefore reports its own score alongside the specific gaps that hold it down, and every score carries components so a reader can open the number and see what produced it. 'publishable' is a hard flag, and when it is false the report must say plainly why, in a sentence a non-specialist can read. Scores here measure the state of Aleph's evidence, never the merits of the document or of any actor; all dimensions are higher_is_better.

overall_state.description: 'insufficient' means Aleph must publish nothing but the gaps themselves. 'partial' means findings may be shown with their limits stated on the same screen, not in a footnote. 'ready' means the evidence base supports the conclusions drawn.

overall_score.description: Weighted aggregate of the dimension scores. A summary of the dimensions, never a substitute for reading them: a high average with one blocking gap is still blocked.

polarity.description: Fixed for this report so the UI can never mis-colour readiness scores.

blocking_gaps.description: Gaps severe enough to prevent publication on their own. Listed at the top level, not buried in a dimension, because a single missing primary source can invalidate an otherwise well-covered analysis.

publishable.description: Whether Aleph may present verdicts and scores for this document. False whenever any blocking gap remains. This flag is decided by evidence coverage alone; no level of model confidence may flip it.

why_not_publishable.description: Plain-language explanation, addressed to a reader rather than a developer, of what is missing and what would fix it. MUST be a non-empty string whenever publishable is false - a refusal without a stated reason is indistinguishable from a failure. Null only when publishable is true.

confidence.description: Evidence confidence in this readiness assessment itself, with model_confidence recorded separately and subordinate. If these two diverge, the evidence figure governs.

phase_status.description: Completion state of each of the seven warm phases. A phase that failed or was skipped is a documented reason for low readiness rather than an unexplained low score.

recommended_actions.description: Concrete retrieval or extraction steps that would raise readiness, ordered by expected effect. The output of this file should be a work list, not a verdict on the document.

allOf.$comment: Enforces the product rule that a refusal must always be explained: publishable=false requires a non-empty why_not_publishable.

gap.description: One specific, named hole in the evidence base. Gaps are written to be actionable: 'no independent estimate of the cost figure' is a gap, 'more research needed' is not. Naming the resolving evidence is what turns a low score into a task.

dimension.description: Which readiness dimension this gap sits under.

description.description: What is missing, stated specifically enough that someone could go and get it.

severity.description: 'blocking' means nothing may be published while it stands. 'major' means findings may be shown only with the limitation displayed alongside them. 'minor' is recorded for completeness.

missing_kind.description: What sort of material is absent. Typed so the retrieval planner can act on it automatically.

what_would_resolve.description: The specific artefact or retrieval that would close the gap. Null only when nothing available could close it, which is itself a publishable finding.

affected_claim_ids.description: Claims or propositions that cannot be evaluated while this gap stands.

dimension_score.description: One readiness dimension. Carries its own components so the number is inspectable, its weight so the aggregate is reproducible, a rationale in plain language, and the gaps that are holding it down. A dimension may never be reported as a bare number.

score.description: 0-100, higher is better. Measures Aleph's evidence coverage on this dimension - not the quality of the document and not the conduct of any actor.

weight.description: Contribution of this dimension to overall_score. Published so the aggregate can be recomputed and challenged.

rationale.description: Why the score is what it is, in language a reader can check against the components.

components.description: The inspectable contributors to this score. Required by Aleph's rule that no metric exists without its components; an empty array is only valid for a dimension scored zero for total absence of material.

gaps.description: What is missing on this dimension.

dimensions.description: The seven readiness dimensions, all required. Fixed keys rather than an open list: a dimension that could be omitted would be omitted precisely when it scored badly, and the absence would read as adequacy.

document_understanding.description: How completely the source document itself was read: text quality, section coverage, provisions and assumptions extracted. Everything else rests on this, so a low score here caps the rest.

primary_source_coverage.description: Whether the underlying official documents, records and datasets were retrieved, rather than only commentary about them. Reporting about a document is not the document.

news_coverage.description: Volume and breadth of retrieved reporting. Deliberately not the leading dimension: abundant coverage of a subject is not evidence about it, and a well-covered story with no primary sources is still unready.

temporal_coverage.description: Whether evidence spans the periods that matter - before and after the document, and the dates its own provisions turn on. A snapshot from one week cannot support a claim about a trend.

evidence_diversity.description: Spread across evidence TIERS and viewpoints: official, statistical, academic, journalistic, and material that cuts against the document's own account. Measures the shape of the evidence set, never the balance of opinions in it.

claim_coverage.description: Proportion of extracted claims that have any evidence attached at all. Uncovered claims must be shown as unevaluated rather than quietly dropped.

source_independence.description: How much of the retrieved material is independent observation rather than restatement. Ten outlets running one wire story is one source; without this dimension, syndication reads as corroboration and inflates every other number.

evidence_inventory.description: Raw counts behind the dimension scores, so a reader can sanity-check a percentage against the underlying totals instead of taking it on trust.

independent_sources.description: Distinct originating sources after syndicated and derivative items are collapsed.

item_count.description: How many items the phase produced, e.g. propositions or evidence records.

note.description: Why a phase failed or was skipped. A skipped phase with no note is an unexplained gap and should be treated as a failure.
